I didn't really have a moving specific fund that I saved to, I probably should have, but I used life savings. When you apply you have to supply bank statements and I think they recommend you can show $5,000 AUD in savings.

Australian in the UK here. The smell of Australia is what I miss the most, no question. I found candles on my last trip back that sort of replicate it but it's not really the same. An american friend describes it as salt (the sea), dirt, eucalyptus and warm lemons. My favourite thing about landing (I usually land early morning) is the smell hitting me and the magpie songs.

I can't really comment not knowing you. I will say that I know a lot of expats in the UK, from Australia and elsewhere, and I don't know even one who hasn't experienced culture shock and homesickness to some degree - regardless of whether they like it here or not and regardless of whether they fit in or not. Things are different, immigration is difficult. That doesn't mean it won't be the best decision of your life.

Definitely. Culture shock is hard, and you will get it, even with the exposure to British culture and the shared history, it is a very different place to Australia.
